objective: Add two repository-only skills in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-req (branch release/0.3.0/feat/requirements-tree): .claude/skills/requirements/ for creating, adjusting and removing instruction requirements and translating them per model family, and .claude/skills/write-skills/ for writing the skills HolyAgent distributes to the Agent Skills standard so they work on every supported model family.
scope: Work only in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-req. A parallel writer is turning packages/runtime/src/instructions/requirements.md and requirements/*.md into a requirements/ tree that mirrors the claude-5.5/ tree file for file (requirements/<path>.md holds the id-led requirements that become <family>/<path>.md), adding claude-5.5/guide.md and kimi-k3.1/guide.md, a supported-families list in code (claude-5.5 now; kimi-k3.1 joins with its translations in a later PR), the package script `instructions:scaffold` in packages/runtime (delegating to a mise task; it creates missing same-named empty files and directories in each family and never overwrites), mirror and id-coverage tests, and packages/runtime/AGENTS.md. Refer to those by those paths and names; read their current state in the worktree if present, but do not edit them.

requirements skill (.claude/skills/requirements/SKILL.md, plus references/ if useful): create, adjust and remove a requirement (ids, which requirements/ file, moving a file), then run `bunx --no-install mise run instructions:scaffold` (or `bun run instructions:scaffold` in packages/runtime) after creating or moving a requirements file and before writing each family's translation; translate into each listed family following that family's guide.md; remove the family files when a requirements file is removed; rebuild with `bunx --no-install mise run build` and run `bunx --no-install mise run verify`. The maintainer said the scaffold script must be used in this skill.

write-skills skill (.claude/skills/write-skills/SKILL.md plus references/): how to write the skills HolyAgent ships (they live in packages/runtime/src/instructions/<family>/skills/<skill>/). Follow the Agent Skills standard: SKILL.md frontmatter (name, description; the optional fields), directory layout, progressive disclosure, references/, scripts/, assets/, size guidance. Put the relevant parts of the standard in its own reference files, from /home/user/holyagent-notes/agent-skills-standard.md with source links. Take the guidance shared by and complementary between the model guides (/home/user/holyagent-notes/claude-guide-points.md and /home/user/holyagent-notes/kimi-guide-points.md, which become claude-5.5/guide.md and kimi-k3.1/guide.md) so a distributed skill works on every supported family; prefer shared points, and where the guides differ say how to write text that satisfies both. Keep the repository rule from .claude/CLAUDE.md: a skill description starts with the situation, then what the skill does.
Both skills are specific to this repository and are not distributed: they live under .claude/skills/ only, never under packages/. Each description starts with the situation, then what the skill does.
Write instruction text in English, terse, with the reason beside each rule; follow the instruction-writing skill at packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/instruction-writing/SKILL.md.
constraints: Every maintainer requirement of the Intent in use is binding; add no behavior it does not name.
Write only under .claude/skills/; never edit .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json or packages/.
Make no version-control writes; report the changed paths.

criteria.text: The requirements skill covers create, adjust and remove, runs the scaffold script before translating, translates per each family's guide.md, and names the build and verify gates

The write-skills skill follows the Agent Skills standard with its relevant parts in reference files with sources, and draws on the shared and complementary model-guide points so skills work on every supported family
Both skills live only under .claude/skills/, are not distributed, and their descriptions start with the situation
